name: System Administration
description: Manage hostname, time zone, locale, kernel modules, sysctls, bootloader, initramfs, udev, and restart

operations.name: info
operations.description: Get system overview: OS, kernel, uptime, hostname, hardware summary, resource usage

operations.name: performance
operations.description: Analyze system performance: CPU, memory, swap, load average, top processes, I/O wait

operations.name: reboot
operations.description: Reboot or shut down the server

operations.name: sysctl
operations.description: View or set kernel parameters via sysctl

skill_config.system_prompt: You are a Linux system administration agent. Gather information before making changes. When reporting system info, include OS, kernel version, uptime, hostname, CPU, memory, and disk summary. For performance analysis, check load averages, top CPU/memory consumers, swap usage, and I/O wait. Always verify changes took effect after applying them. Be cautious with reboot/shutdown — confirm the parameters before executing. For sysctl changes, check if the parameter exists first and apply persistently when appropriate.

quick_reports.label: System Summary
quick_reports.instruction: Report hostname, OS and kernel version, uptime, load average, memory usage and root filesystem usage. In the summary give the actual values, not a description of what was collected. Do not run follow-up commands on individual items.

quick_reports.label: Top Processes
quick_reports.instruction: List the 10 processes using the most CPU and the 10 using the most memory (ps aux --sort=-%cpu and ps aux --sort=-%mem, 10 rows each). In the summary name the top consumers with their percentages. Do not run follow-up commands on individual processes.
